name: Queen's Gambit
goal: As White, you can offer the c-pawn with the Queen's Gambit, and win it back while you develop when Black takes it.
intro: The Queen's Gambit starts 1.d4 d5 2.c4. White offers the c-pawn, not to give it away, but to tempt Black's d-pawn out of the centre. Here Black takes it with 2...dxc4, and you win the pawn back simply by bringing out your pieces, then castle with the bigger share of the centre.

parts.title: Win the pawn back while you develop
parts.keyIdea: Offer a side pawn to pull Black's d-pawn out of the centre, then win it back with moves that develop your pieces.
parts.text: You are White, from the first move. The line is the main line as Lichess's list of openings names it. At each move, ask what it does for your centre, your pieces and your king.
parts.line: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3 Nf6 Bxc4 e6 Nf3 c5 O-O a6

notes.text: 1.d4 claims the centre with a pawn that your queen already guards, and it opens a path for the bishop on c1. The Engine rates 1.d4 and 1.e4 almost the same.

2.c4 is the Queen's Gambit. It attacks the d5 pawn from the side: if Black takes, the d-pawn has left the centre, and Black usually cannot keep the extra pawn for long. Black can also turn it down with 2...e6 or 2...c6.
Black has taken the pawn, so there is no longer a Black pawn on d5 to fight for e4. 3.e3 opens a diagonal for the bishop on f1, which can now take back on c4. 3.Nf3 and 3.e4 are good too.

4.Bxc4 wins the pawn back and develops a piece in one move. Black could not easily have kept it: after 3...b5 4.a4 c6 5.axb5 cxb5, the queen jumps to f3 and attacks the rook on a8 along the long diagonal, and Black loses a piece.
Material is level again, so keep developing. 5.Nf3 brings out a knight that guards d4 and watches e5, and it clears the way for your king to castle.

5...c5 hits your d4 pawn: this is how Black fights back in the centre. Castle first with 6.O-O, so your king is safe before lines open. Black often goes on with ...a6 and ...b5 to push your bishop back, and it can step back to b3 or e2.
